newsitem.title: CHINA: China Jiangsu refining lag boosts oil product price.
newsitem.headline: China Jiangsu refining lag boosts oil product price.

text.p: Prices of petroleum products in China's eastern Jiangsu province are seen continuing to rise amid mounting seasonal demand and lower output from the Nanjing refinery, the Market Daily said on Thursday.
Repairs and installation of new equipment at the refinery had caused substantial cuts in production of petrol, the newspaper said without elaborating.
Output of petrol had fallen in the province while demand was rising as farmers started their spring planting and construction on several major projects got under way, the newspaper said.
"Forecasts are that demand for finished petroleum products will further increase in the near future and prices will continue their rising trend," it said.
Output of 70-octane-grade petrol in the province had fallen since the start of April, raising the wholesale price by 60 yuan ($7.23) to 2,480 yuan a tonne, it said.
The wholesale price of 90-grade petrol had risen by 100 yuan to 2,680 yuan a tonne and other grades had seen smaller price increases, it said.
In a separate report, the newspaper said prices of some oil products in southern Guangdong province were falling, due mainly to increased imports and lower production costs.
The price of heavy oil in the province had fallen by more than 200 yuan a tonne since the beginning of the year, the newspaper said.
Grade 20 fuel oil was selling for 1,240 yuan a tonne while 380-grade heavy oil was priced at 1,220 yuan a tonne, it said.
China had imported more than 2.31 million tonnes of fuel oil in the first quarter in 1997, a rise of more than 54 percent from the same period last year, it said.
Much of those imports had been shipped through Guangdong, it said without giving further details.
